purpose: Machine-readable mirror of skill/SKILL.md for the OpenCode arm. Read by scripts/check_policy_sync.py (rule blocks must equal SKILL.md verbatim) and scripts/check_opencode_pool.py (the 19-model pool with its budget/free/premium/Gemini tiers, the Step 4-OC rows and the badge table must match SKILL.md). Not read by the router.
drift_guard: Change a rule block here and forget SKILL.md, or the reverse, and check_policy_sync.py fails. The iteration-20 mirror, reachability corpus and matrix audited the retired Codex arm; they were removed from the tree and last exist at commit 7c24c81 (archive/iteration-20-codex/).

rule_blocks.note: Each body must equal the text between <!-- rule:ID --> and <!-- /rule:ID --> in skill/SKILL.md, verbatim.

blocks.S0: **S0 · blocked output.** A prompt blocked at Step 0 emits exactly one line, a `Clarify:` line naming the missing information as a question, and no `Claude:`, `OpenCode:`, `Evidence:` or badge line at all.
blocks.D3DIAG: **D3DIAG · diagnosis.** The coding column is written for building, so debugging scores on its own test: bounded diagnosis is `D=2`, and adversarial diagnosis is `D=3` when at least two of these hold — the root cause is non-local or depends on timing or ordering; reproduction is intermittent or environment-dependent; several plausible causes must be ruled out by constructing competing hypotheses; a local-looking fix could mask a deeper invariant violation.
blocks.M1: **M1 · `max`.** Emit `max` only when `D = 3` and `R = 3` and the model is a flagship (Opus 5.5 / Opus 4.8 / Fable 5.2 / Mythos 5.2) and the difficulty is one indivisible novel-design or formal decision. Otherwise `xhigh`.
blocks.A1: **A1 · frontier rung.** Opus 5.5 becomes Fable 5.2 only when the dominant capability is on the flagship list and `A = high`, where `A = high` means the user states that an earlier flagship-tier run at `xhigh` or `max` already fell short. A long or unattended session is not that statement.
blocks.O1: **O1 · orchestration load.** `O = high` when the session must run three or more distinct phases, where a phase is a stretch of work that produces a different kind of deliverable and whose output is consumed by a later phase. The phases that count are research, implementation, independent verification, packaging, data or schema migration, documentation, and triage. The whole edit-run-repair implementation loop is one phase, and tests you write for your own change are inside it.
blocks.UC1: **UC1 · `ultracode`.** Emit `ultracode` when the estimated duration is over 30 minutes and either `O = high` or (`W = 3` and `D >= 2`) and the difficulty is not one indivisible chain. Write it as a flag after the effort, `effort: <level> · ultracode`, where the level is the Effort ← D rung with a floor of `high` and a ceiling of `xhigh`. Never on Haiku 5.5.
blocks.B1: **B1 · evidence applicability.** A benchmark row takes part in the badge decision only if the capability it measures is one of the dominant tags named for this prompt in Step 2. Applicability is checked before evidence quality and before any tie-break, and a row that is not applicable does not enter the comparison at all, however strong its number.
blocks.BD1: **BD1 · direction without an interval.** A badge direction needs at least two independent measurements that agree — an independent evaluator's run, or a vendor's table that favours its rival — at least one of them tier A or B, and none that disagree. The same benchmark re-published on a second page is one measurement, a tie is not opposition, and an aggregate never counts. Otherwise the cell is decided by efficiency, except at R = 3, where a single admissible measurement still decides it: a lean is not parity.
blocks.MECH1: **MECH1 · mechanism rows.** `ultracode` driven by `O = high`, or a task routed to `opusplan`, names something OpenCode does not have, so it decides the badge for Claude unless the other capability row carries a benchmark direction under BD1, which wins.
blocks.NC1: **NC1 · non-confidential unlock.** Only when the user says the work is non-confidential or personal: GPT 6 Luna stays in the pool (30-day retention is accepted; Grok 4.7 stays premium under BUD1 and does not return), and Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor takes `#2` on `research-synthesis` rows only (AA-Omniscience 25 vs MiMo-V2.6-Pro 8, USD 60 cap against USD 15) — except in the right-hand column, where Rule GM1 already puts Gemini 4 Argon at `#1` and the row's former `#1` stays `#2`. Never infer non-confidentiality from the prompt's tone.
blocks.PO1: **PO1 · pair order.** At `D ≤ 2` and `R ≤ 2` the most cap-efficient model inside the leading consensus band goes first; at `D = 3` or `R = 3` the leader on the hardest anchors goes first (the right-hand column). This orders the pair only — the badge still follows SM1.
blocks.CAP1: **CAP1 · cap rule.** The USD 15-cap budget models (MiMo-V2.6-Pro, GPT 6 Luna) are reserved for `D ≥ 2`; `D ≤ 1` goes to the USD 60–80-cap Flash tier (the `latency-volume` row is exempt). Caps are per model: when the user says a model's window is exhausted, name the next model of its chain in `Evidence:` only — Pro **MiMo-V2.6-Pro → DeepSeek V4.1 Flash → GLM-5.3-Flash**; Flash **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash → GLM-5.3-Flash → MiMo-V2.6-Flash**.
blocks.A1-OC: **A1-OC · escalation rung.** When the user states that an earlier OpenCode run fell short, `#2` becomes the premium model with the best consensus for the dominant capability — **GLM-5.3** for `agentic-code`, `terminal-tool`, `workflow-automation` and `research-synthesis`; **Kimi K3.1 Pro** for `deep-reasoning`, `science`, `long-context` and `doc-data-understanding` (Kimi K3 has no AA v5 row, so there is no same-version comparison and `Evidence:` says `low-confidence`); **Qwen3.8 Max** for `knowledge-work` — except that **Gemini 4 Argon** takes `#2` on the GM1 rows at `D = 2` with `R ≤ 2` (at `D = 3` or `R = 3` it is already `#1`, so `#2` stays the premium model of the tag), and **Grok 4.7** comes in elsewhere when the work is non-confidential (NC1) — and `Evidence:` names its cost (about 3–8% of its monthly cap per real agent task, Grok 10%, Argon about 3% of its USD 30 cap per task at today's half price). After a shortfall at `D ≥ 2` the badge goes to Claude whenever the dominant capability has a Claude cell anywhere in the badge table — `agentic-code`, `terminal-tool`, `deep-reasoning`, `knowledge-work`, whatever the task's own depth — because the earlier run already showed the task is harder than the OpenCode pair handles; at `D = 3` also say the Claude line is stronger.
blocks.H1: **H1 · Haiku 5.5.** Haiku 5.5 is the Claude pick when `R ≤ 1` and `C ≤ 1` and the dominant capability is not `research-synthesis` and one of these holds: `D = 0` and `W = 0`; or `D = 1` and `W ≤ 1` and the dominant capability is `instruction-following`, `latency-volume`, or none of the tags fits (a summary, a reformat, a translation, a label, a rewrite or an answer from text the user provides). Effort is `low` at `D = 0` and `medium` at `D = 1`, never higher.
blocks.H2: **H2 · Haiku escalation.** When the user says an earlier Haiku 5.5 run fell short, or asks for more care on work H1 would give Haiku, the Claude line becomes Sonnet 5.5 at its own `D` rung. Haiku's effort is never raised instead.
blocks.BUD1: **BUD1 · budget-first pool.** The five premium models — GLM-5.3, Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1 Pro, Grok 4.7 and Qwen3.8 Max (tier **P**) — are never `#1` or `#2` of a routed pair. They reach the OpenCode line only through Rule A1-OC, after the user states that an earlier OpenCode run fell short. Every other pair is built from the budget tier (tier **B**: MiMo-V2.6-Pro, GLM-5.3-Flash, MiMo-V2.6-Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), Gemini 4 Argon where Rule GM1 allows it, and, under NC1, GPT 6 Luna and Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor. Tier membership is by name, not by a tasks-per-month threshold (the `tasks/mo` column is informational — Arena snapshot of 8 Nov 2026). Qwen3.8 Flash is unrated — no independent row for the served model — so it is never `#1` or `#2` either.
blocks.SM1: **SM1 · OpenCode by default.** The badge goes to OpenCode unless Claude clears a serious margin. Claude takes it only when a hard gate or the context window puts OpenCode out, or MECH1 applies, or `D = 3` and the dominant capability is `agentic-code`, `terminal-tool` or `deep-reasoning` and BD1 gives Claude a direction, or the dominant capability is `knowledge-work` at `D ≥ 2` with a BD1 direction, or `R = 3` and `D ≥ 2` and the dominant row leans to Claude. Every `D ≤ 1` task and every other `D = 2` task is OpenCode: the budget pair clears the bar there, and a Claude direction that only shows on harder tasks is not a reason to spend Claude's quota.
blocks.FR1: **FR1 · free lane.** No free model on Go has a measured score, so none is ever `#1` or `#2`: MiniMax M3.1 Flash Free left Go (Go now lists the paid MiniMax M3.1 Flash at a USD 20 cap — never selected, no independent row for that listing), Beam Free (30-day retention) and LongCat 2.5 Free (hosted in China) are unmeasured, and Iceman Contributor Free trains on prompts. Zen's free twins of paid Flash models (`glm-5.3-flash-free`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, `minimax-m3.1-flash-free`: same base models, zero retention, no training, free for a limited time; context windows n/p) are never `#1` or `#2` either — when the user says a paid Flash window is exhausted, `Evidence:` names the twin before the CAP1 chain. `mimo-v2.6-flash-free` trains on prompts (NC1 spill-over only). Every other free model is never selected.
blocks.GM1: **GM1 · Gemini slot.** Gemini 4 Argon (`opencode-go/gemini-4-argon`) is on Go's privacy table as not trained on, with 0-day retention, so it is open to confidential work; its Go cap is USD 30 and, at today's 50%-off prices, it buys about 38 real agent tasks a month (about 19 once list prices return on 1 Dec 2026), so it never takes a slot at `D ≤ 2` with `R ≤ 2`. In the right-hand column (`D = 3` or `R = 3`) it is `#1`, effort `high`, on `agentic-code`, `terminal-tool`, `deep-reasoning`, `research-synthesis` and `workflow-automation` — the rows where independent evidence puts it above the budget tier — and the row's former `#1` becomes `#2`. After an OpenCode shortfall at `D = 2` with `R ≤ 2` it is `#2` on the same rows (Rule A1-OC); at `D = 3` or `R = 3` it is already `#1`. If it errors or is overloaded, run the row's other model.
